name: quick-exit
title: Quick exit
description: A quick exit for sensitive services: one button always in view, or Escape three times, blanks the page and replaces it with a neutral site.
docs: Put it first in your layout, so the first Tab reaches it, and pass href, the neutral site (required: pick one that is ordinary for your audience, a weather page or a news site). The button, Leave this site now by default (label), stays in a corner of the window (placement) on every page, 44px tall on a phone. Pressing it, or Escape three times within a second (shortcut, { key, presses, within } or false), blanks the page at once with a plain surface and nothing from your site on it, then replaces the current history entry with the neutral address (hideHistory, default true), so Back does not return, and opens it in the same tab. The button is named by what it says and described as Quick exit, opens a neutral site, with the shortcut added (labels). The Escape count ignores presses that came from inside a dialog, a menu or an open list, and presses that something already handled, so it never fights a dialog that closes on Escape; it counts in text fields, because someone typing a form must be able to leave. Each press shows on the button as Esc x3, x2, x1. onExit(event) runs a moment before the page goes, with the reason (button or keyboard) and the href: use it to clear a draft or a session, call event.preventDefault() to take over in a preview or a test, and keep analytics out of it. A browser still keeps its history and the page may show in an app switcher: say so on the page that explains how to stay safe.
